newsitem.title: FRANCE: Most French reckon too many Arabs in France - report.
newsitem.headline: Most French reckon too many Arabs in France - report.

text.p: Nearly two-thirds of French people think there are too many Arabs in their country even though most deplore racism and see it as a threat to France, a human rights report suggested on Friday.
"Xenophobia -- in other words, hatred of foreigners, is on a dangerous rise," France's National Consultative Commission on Human Rights said in an annual report.
Its survey showed that 61 percent of French people questioned felt there were too many Arabs, 58 percent thought there were too many Moslems and 38 percent too many blacks in France.

Seventy-nine percent said the behaviour of some immigrants justified racist reactions. The figures comfort the anti-immigrant extreme-right National Front party, which won control of a fourth town in a municipal election last month.

"French society is racked by a xenophobic current which, throughout the years, is expressed with increasing openness. The taboo is being eroded in the face of citizens' weakening resistance," it said.

However, a majority of those questioned felt that racism posed a threat to the country, although they placed it seventh behind their worries about unemployment, poverty, exclusion, AIDS, drugs and insecurity.
And 70 percent felt that people found guilty by courts of racist acts do not receive sufficiently harsh punishment.
"This racism is massively recognised and deplored by the French people questioned in the survey. They see it as a threat weighing on France," the commission said.
The survey, conducted in November, questioned 1,049 people over 18 years of age.

Thirty percent of the participants felt there were too many Asians and 20 percent answered there were too many Jews, yet 76 percent of those question said they found east European immigrants likeable.
The commission also noted a decline in the number of racist attacks since 1995, when seven people died and two were hurt. In 1996, just two people were hurt in racially-motivated assaults.

It pointed out that 21 attacks were carried out against North Africans on the Mediterranean island of Corsica while only seven occurred on mainland France in 1996. France counts some three million mostly North African immigrants.
Anti-Semitic violence was in clear decline.
